Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral widening of the lower posterior mediastinum with smooth, lateral displacement of both paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads), a classic radiographic sign of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the paravertebral regions. The absence of vertebral destruction helps distinguish this from metastatic disease or infection, and the bilateral symmetric nature makes a solitary neurogenic tumor unlikely.
